plan.title: 2x2 genotype x treatment DESeq2 interaction analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question — does the drug act differently in KO than in WT — is an interaction question in a 2x2 factorial design (genotype: WT/KO x treatment: vehicle/drug, n=4 per cell, 16 samples total, human brain tissue, 12000-gene salmon count matrix of unstated length-correction state). This requires a DESeq2 model with the full interaction term genotype:treatment, not two separate two-group comparisons. The plan: (1) confirm sample structure via blind VST/PCA before any modeling, (2) minimally pre-filter, fit DESeq2 with design ~genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, test the interaction coefficient (the 'does the drug act differently' term) with the Wald test, then report the two simple effects (drug vs vehicle within WT; drug vs vehicle within KO) alongside the interaction contrast, (3) shrink each contrast's log2FC with ashr (interaction/simple effects are not single coefficients so apeglm is not appropriate), (4) BH-adjust within each contrast, (5) run fgsea preranked enrichment per contrast (interaction, WT simple effect, KO simple effect) against MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome and WikiPathways (all human, present in the reference store), (6) integrate into one report with diagnostics, simple-effects/interaction table, and enrichment results. The counts are delivered as a gene-level table from salmon with no per-sample quantification files or transcript-length table provided, so the length offset cannot be reconstructed; the model runs on the counts as delivered and this caveat is stated in the report per the grounded guidance. All steps and settings are grounded against the cited procedure (snapshot sha256:40605ae4...); the knowledge_check call confirmed no violations for the final step set.

DESeq2 Wald test: interaction term genotypeKO.treatmentdrug, plus simple effects (drug vs vehicle in WT; drug vs vehicle in KO)
ashr shrinkage on each contrast
Benjamini-Hochberg within each contrast, independent filtering on, alpha 0.05
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, per contrast, Hallmark then Reactome and WikiPathways
Integrated report with simple effects, interaction contrast, diagnostics, enrichment tables

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
